rationales: This is the expansion of ASCII: American Standard Code for Information Interchange.
ASCII stands for American, not Advanced, Standard Code for Information Interchange.
ASCII uses “Code,” not “Communication,” in its name.
ASCII uses “American” and “Code,” not “Advanced” and “Communication.”

Standard ASCII uses 7 bits per character.
Eight bits are used by extended ASCII representations, not standard ASCII.
Standard ASCII does not use 16 bits per character.
Standard ASCII does not use 32 bits per character.
Unicode can use more storage than ASCII, so using fewer bits is not its key advantage.
Unicode supports characters from many languages and writing systems beyond ASCII’s limited character set.
Binary is a way of representing data, not a compatibility property that distinguishes Unicode from ASCII.
Unicode is not specific to English; it supports characters from many languages.
One byte is generally too small for a typical integer representation.
Two bytes may be used in some systems, but are not the typical size assumed here.
A typical integer is commonly stored in 4 bytes.
Eight bytes are commonly used for larger or 64-bit integers, rather than a typical integer.
Unsigned integers represent zero and positive values, whereas signed integers can also represent negative values.
Signed integers do not generally have a larger range of positive values than unsigned integers of the same width.
Unsigned integers are stored as integer values, not in floating-point format.
Signed integers can represent negative as well as positive values.
Twenty-three bits are used for the single-precision fraction, not the exponent.
Single precision allocates 8 bits to the exponent.
Eleven exponent bits are used in double precision.
Fifty-two bits are used for the double-precision fraction, not the single-precision exponent.

Pixels are the tiny picture elements that make up a digital image.
Bits are units of digital information, not the name for the image’s tiny dots.
Bytes are groups of bits, not the name for the image’s tiny dots.
Nodes are points or devices in some kinds of networks or graphs, not image dots.
RGB stands for Red, Green, Blue.
Gray and Black are not the words represented by the G and B in RGB.
“Right” is not the word represented by R in RGB.
Brown is not the word represented by B in RGB.
